mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has risen 7 percentage points from t-3w to t-0w (−53.0 to −46.0), signaling gradual return-to-office behavior. This sustained upward trend in workplace attendance will drive commuting-adjacent retail visits over the next four weeks, lifting RETAIL_REC above its recent baseline.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from −53.0% to −46.0% over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the mean of the prior 28 days, or WORKPLACES reverses by more than 5 percentage points in week t+1.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has declined from 21.1% to 18.1% over four weeks, indicating reduced home-confinement intensity. As people spend less time at home, discretionary retail-and-recreation visits will increase proportionally over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility increases above 19.0% in week t+1, or RETAIL_REC does not rise relative to its four-week mean.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT station mobility remains severely depressed at −61.0%, indicating public-transport avoidance. If TRANSIT falls an additional 5 percentage points or more in week t+1, consumers will substitute toward personal-vehicle retail trips, but the overall retail-and-recreation category will contract due to reduced foot traffic density in commercial hubs.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 5 percentage points week-on-week from t-0w baseline
failure_condition: TRANSIT improves by more than 3 percentage points in week t+1, or RETAIL_REC rises despite further TRANSIT decline.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility shows high volatility (−2.7%, +18.3%, −2.6%, −2.0%), indicating weather or policy-driven outdoor-activity swings. When PARKS exceeds −5.0% and RESIDENTIAL falls below 19.5% simultaneously, consumers redirect discretionary time from home to outdoor recreation rather than indoor retail, suppressing RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: PARKS falls below −10.0% in week t+1, or RETAIL_REC increases despite the interaction condition being met.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has improved from −19.7% to −12.6% over four weeks, indicating relaxed restrictions on essential retail. This improvement signals broader policy easing. If GROCERY_PHARM continues to improve by more than 3 percentage points in week t+1, non-essential retail restrictions will also ease, driving RETAIL_REC upward over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM improves more than 3 percentage points from t-0w in week t+1
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM stalls or declines in week t+1, or RETAIL_REC remains below −60% despite GROCERY_PHARM improvement.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT are both severely depressed (−46.0% and −61.0% respectively) and show correlated improvement patterns. When both series improve by at least 3 percentage points simultaneously in week t+1, it signals coordinated reopening of employment and transport infrastructure, which will lift RETAIL_REC over the subsequent four weeks through increased commuter foot traffic.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES improves ≥3 points AND TRANSIT improves ≥3 points in week t+1
evidence_refs: fact:both series show sustained improvement trend
failure_condition: Either WORKPLACES or TRANSIT declines in week t+1, or RETAIL_REC does not rise above −60% despite both proxies improving.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility spiked to +18.3% in week t-2w, indicating strong seasonal outdoor-activity demand. If PARKS returns to positive territory (>0%) in week t+1 and RESIDENTIAL remains below 19.0%, consumers will allocate discretionary time to parks rather than indoor retail venues, causing RETAIL_REC to decline or stagnate over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: PARKS remains negative in week t+1, or RETAIL_REC rises above −62% despite positive PARKS and low RESIDENTIAL.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has stabilized at approximately −63% over the past three weeks (−65.0%, −62.9%, −63.4%, −63.0%), indicating a steady-state equilibrium under current restrictions. Absent a shock to WORKPLACES (>−40%) or TRANSIT (>−50%), RETAIL_REC will remain within the −62% to −64% band over the next four weeks, producing a direction of zero or minimal change.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES remains below −40% AND TRANSIT remains below −50% throughout t+1 to t+4
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC stable at −63% ±1.5 for three weeks
failure_condition: WORKPLACES exceeds −40% or TRANSIT exceeds −50% in any week t+1 to t+4, or RETAIL_REC rises above −60%.
